title: Irreducible fast sets of bump homeomorphisms generate copies of Thompson's groups $F_n$
summary: A homeomorphism of an interval is a positive bump if its support is a single open interval on which it moves every point to the right. Choosing a fundamental domain $[m,b(m))$ for the action of a positive bump $b$ on its support splits the remainder of the support into two intervals, called the feet of $b$. A finite set of positive bumps is geometrically fast if fundamental domains can be chosen so that all the resulting feet are pairwise disjoint.
